title: Mouse Without Borders connection to a managed work laptop fails

status.label: Confirm managed firewall authorization
status.detail: The author clarified that the work laptop cannot approve firewall prompts. A network-policy cause is plausible, not proven; the proposed focused question has not been posted.

next_action.label: Request IT-approved inbound-connection result
next_action.reason: An authorized firewall verdict separates managed-network restrictions from a remaining Mouse Without Borders defect without asking the user to bypass policy.

judgment.rationale: The author answered the broad setup ambiguity: same-network attempts, IP mapping and VPN changes did not help, and firewall authorization prompts could not be approved. Whether the failing inbound attempt is actually blocked remains unknown.
evidence: 0.71.0 report describes Windows 11/Windows 10 directional connectivity and a work laptop without administrator credentials.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/27367#issuecomment-2230350958 clarifies prior successful use, unsuccessful IP mapping, same-network tests and unapproved firewall prompts.
The earlier Easy Mouse suggestion is from another user's experience, not confirmation of this reporter's root cause.
Current Settings exposes AddFirewallRule as an add_firewall custom action; managed firewall authorization is not something a client should bypass.
Tracker #51077 groups this open unassigned report, but supplies no concrete fix attempt.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for an IT-admin-confirmed allow/block result for the failing main-PC-to-work-laptop connection; reopen code investigation if the authorized path is clear.

fix_assessment.rationale: The presently documented obstacle is authorization of a managed laptop's inbound firewall access, which must be resolved by its administrator rather than by bypassing policy in PowerToys. This is a conditional external-configuration disposition, not a confirmed firewall diagnosis: a clear approved path would warrant renewed product investigation.

issue_context.summary: A previously working two-PC setup now fails toward a managed Windows 10 laptop; its user lacks credentials to approve firewall prompts and has already tried same-network, VPN and IP-mapping comparisons.
known_information: The edited body and July reply correct the initial ambiguous description.
The work laptop lacks administrator credentials even though the original form marked running as admin.
The user reports unapproved firewall prompts, no improvement from IP mapping, and failure with or without VPN on the same network.
No maintainer request is currently awaiting an author response; this new question remains a draft.
inferences: Blocked inbound access could explain directional failure, but no firewall log or authorized connection test confirms that.
The other commenter's Easy Mouse solution should not be asserted as this reporter's solution.
issue_context.analysis: Ask only for the missing administrator-verifiable discriminator. Do not request credentials, pair keys, blanket firewall disabling, or repeat the already supplied VPN/IP-mapping experiments.
initial_investigation: Read the complete edited report, both comments, tracker cross-reference and matching PR search.
Inspected MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.AddFirewallRule and its add_firewall action; the existence of this action does not prove the reporter has a permitted inbound rule.

information_gaps.information: An IT-authorized allow/block verdict for the failing main-PC-to-work-laptop Mouse Without Borders connection.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes an unapproved managed inbound firewall path from a product failure on an already permitted path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Ask the work laptop's IT administrator to check the approved inbound Mouse Without Borders rule and the firewall/endpoint-policy event for one timestamped failing connection attempt; share only the allow/block outcome and relevant non-sensitive error.

actions.label: Confirm IT-authorized inbound firewall result

comment.body: Thanks for clarifying that this previously worked, IP mapping did not help, the PCs are on the same network with or without VPN, and the work laptop's firewall prompts could not be approved because you lack administrator credentials. That makes an inbound policy restriction plausible, but does not prove it; the earlier Easy Mouse suggestion does not settle this case. Could you ask your IT administrator to check whether inbound Mouse Without Borders access is approved on the work laptop and inspect the firewall/endpoint-policy result for one timestamped failing main-PC-to-work-laptop connection attempt? Please share just the allow/block outcome and any relevant non-sensitive error, not credentials, pairing keys or private network details. This distinguishes a managed policy block from a product failure on a permitted connection. Do not disable firewall protection or bypass your organization's policy.
